hypotheses.note: E0RegComplete.IsE0C1CompleteCauchy (OQ-142), unchanged; G4 uses only its field reg, the compact part only that S is a closed Cauchy surface

sorries.obstruction: the tail of a Cauchy sequence of Sigma* (locally finite spears, summable radii) lies in a compact set of M. Owed: a comparison, along paths of Sigma* ∩ S, of the induced length of Sigma* (chart system of Reg M) with the DEC-31 length of S (e0SliceSys S), which neither library has. With it the argument is: concatenate a fast Cauchy sequence into a finite-length path Gamma; (a) if a spear is met at arbitrarily late times, its log r estimate gives a compact annulus graph and a convergent subsequence; (b) otherwise replace, spear by spear, first entry to last exit by a rim arc of S-length <= pi R_i (on r = R the printed metric -2dtau dr + dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2 is R^2 dtheta^2), giving an S-path of length <= l(Gamma) + pi sum R_i, which converges by hS.complete and hS.continuous.

proved_this_wave: Sigma* of a locally finite family is spacelike Lipschitz in Reg M (G4), from S spacelike Lipschitz only
Lemma 2.8's log r estimate on Sigma*, spear by spear
a Cauchy sequence of Sigma* with a tail in a compact set converges (the strict compact proof localised)
the spears can be thinned to summable radii
Reg M is Cauchy-complete modulo the one sorry above; regM_isCauchyComplete_of_complete, prop_reg_complete, prop_reg_complete' now rest on it and on nothing else
findings: BTZ_1.tex l.1571 (« the proof of Cauchy-completeness of Proposition prop:abs_max applies as is »): B21's completeness of Sigma* (l.1093, no proof printed) uses finitely many spears (l.1091) and a compact Sigma; with countably many spears the part that is not « as is » is exactly the Cauchy sequences crossing infinitely many spears. The multiplicative comparison between the cusp metric and S's (AUDIT-1's « uniform across spears ») is not needed: on the rim r = R the printed metric -2dtau dr + dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2 restricts to R^2 dtheta^2 whatever tau_Sigma is, so a rim arc has length <= pi R, and choosing spears of summable radii (always possible, LFSurgeryData.exists_summable) turns the comparison into an additive, summable error. The proof should choose the spears' radii; « disjoint spear neighborhoods » (l.1574) alone may not suffice.

The Hopf–Rinow route of T-btz-reg-complete AUDIT-1 finding 2 was not taken: it needs the DEC-31 length topology of S to equal M's near S (hS.continuous gives one direction only) and a Hopf–Rinow–Cohn-Vossen theorem, neither available; the path-surgery route above needs only completeness of S along one path.

kb_proposals: The strict SurgeryData.isSpacelikeLipschitzAt_cusp_interior/_rim and the logRad stack (abs_deriv_logRad_le ... ofReal_abs_logRad_sub_le_edist) need neither finiteness nor compactness: copied verbatim over LFSurgeryData they compile with one change (the union of the other spears is closed by LocallyFinite.comp_injective ... isClosed_iUnion) and hS.reg in place of IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy; a strict clean-up could state them once over LFSurgeryData (finite SurgeryData is a case, sigmaStar_toSurgeryData is rfl).

On the rim r = R of a spear the printed E0 metric -2dtau dr + dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2 is R^2 dtheta^2, whatever the surface: rim arcs have length <= pi R. Thinning spears to summable radii (LFSurgeryData.exists_summable, from posSumOfEncodable) makes errors across infinitely many spears additive and summable.

Completeness of Sigma* reduces to « Cauchy tail in a compact of M » (LFSurgeryData.tendsto_of_cauchySeq_of_isCompact); the missing tool is the comparison of chartSys lengths on Reg M with e0SliceSys lengths on S along common paths.
